newsitem.title: LATVIA: Key Latvia party may quit govt over budget - paper.
newsitem.headline: Key Latvia party may quit govt over budget - paper.

text.p: The leading party in Latvia's ruling coalition, the Democratic Party Saimnieks (DPS), wants changes to the 1997 budget and if its views are not taken into account, it may quit the government, newspaper Diena said on Thursday.
Latvia's 1997 budget has been drawn up without a deficit and has caused much controversy, especially among unions that say public workers are having to make too many sacrifices.
Diena quoted DPS leader Ziedonis Chevers as saying that he, in principle, supported a deficit-free budget but that he could not accept measures going against his party's principles.

He told the newspaper he was especially against the taxation of pensions and the ending of tax relief for families with children, invalids and people who suffered from political repression under the Soviet regime.
He also noted the parliament had not yet accepted legislation that would allow the budget to be financed by such measures.
The DPS is the largest party in the six-party coalition, which Prime Minister Andris Shkele, who himself has no party affiliation, has managed to hold together since December.
The DPS recently ditched leading member Aivar Kreituss, who was then forced to quit as finance minister.
The 1997 budget is part of a package of pledges Latvia made to the International Monetary Fund (IMF) in return for credits.
The 1996 budget deficit is forecast at 40 million lats, after a huge 90 million lat funding gap in 1995 in the wake of a severe banking crisis.
